paragraphs: Lily wanted to thank Sam. He found Pip's red ball in the park. She wanted to make an invitation for a lunch on Saturday. Sam was a kind boy, but he did not say much. But she did not know what Sam liked. "What does he like?" she asked Mia. "Watch him for a day," said Mia. "Then you can guess."

On Monday, Lily and Mia sat in the school canteen. Sam stood in the line for his lunch. Lily had rice and a small salad, but she watched Sam. The board said pasta or pancakes. Sam looked at the pancakes and made a face. "I hate sweet food for lunch," he said. He took the pasta and a glass of water. Lily wrote "pasta" in her little book.

After school, Sam played football on the field. He kicked the ball again and again, and he sang a tune. It was the tune of a football song. Many boys and girls played with him. "Do you like football?" asked Lily. "What do you mean?" said Sam. "I like football more than anything," he said. "I want to play in the next match." Lily wrote "football" in her book and smiled.

On Tuesday, Lily gave Sam the invitation. It said, "Special lunch on Saturday at twelve o'clock. We have pasta, and then we play football." Lily waited and smiled a little. Sam read it and laughed. "How do you know?" he asked. "I watched you," said Lily. "Thank you, Lily," said Sam. "This is a great invitation." Lily guessed right, and Sam was very happy.
